I would **not change Alex’s storage date without written duty-manager permission**. The request is pending, not approved, and later permission cannot retroactively authorise a change.

I would urgently flag the conflict to the manager and warehouse: Claire’s authorised collection is booked for Wednesday, but releasing today’s manifest will send the only copies of the family letters and photographs for irreversible destruction. I would ask for an authorised way to protect the box and get the existing request considered at Tuesday’s sitting.

If there is no authorised way to exclude or protect the box by 13:30, I would **withhold the manifest**, notify the manager that I had done so, and record the reason. That means none of the 60 boxes dispatches today and the shift is incomplete, contrary to the manager’s instruction. It is a substantial disruption, but it avoids irreversible destruction without making an unauthorised date change or concealing the decision.

I would then seek a decision at Tuesday’s sitting. If the extension is approved, I would record it properly and preserve the Wednesday collection, subject to the normal authorised-collector checks. If it is refused, I would seek further management instructions rather than assume the request grants permission.
